paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: God does not leave His people stuck with the name they've been carrying. Zion had been called Forsaken and Desolate, but the LORD says, "you will be called Hephzibah, and your land Beulah" (Isaiah 62:4). And the reason is not that she cleaned herself up first. It's because "the LORD will take delight in you" (Isaiah 62:4).

Now watch what God does with that love. He says, "as a bridegroom rejoices over his bride, so your God will rejoice over you" (Isaiah 62:5). He swears an oath that her hard work will not be taken by strangers, and He promises, "See, your Savior comes!" (Isaiah 62:11). Friend, that's a God who keeps His word, and He even finishes the new name: "Sought Out, A City Not Forsaken" (Isaiah 62:12). Whatever name has been stuck on you, His word about His people is bigger.

And that word gives us something to do while we wait. The watchmen are posted on the walls, and the call goes out to "prepare the way for the people" (Isaiah 62:10). So we keep praying, we keep clearing stones, and we keep our eyes on the road, because a Savior is coming. This is exactly why my ovens stay ready, baker. Nobody knows when (Matthew 24:36), so we get ready with hope, because we are already loved.
